subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For systemd-managed Gateway runs, should config `env.KIMI_API_KEY` be treated as a durable runtime credential source, or should Kimi Coding API keys be stored only through per-agent auth profiles or service env files?
rationale: Both choices affect credential persistence, daemon status semantics, docs, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not pick the permanent provider-secret contract.

options.title: Make config env effective
options.body: Materialize safe config env into the managed Gateway runtime/service context and update status, docs, and tests around that contract.

options.title: Prefer auth profiles or service env
options.body: Update docs and `models status` so config-only env is not presented as effective daemon runtime auth, and steer users to per-agent auth storage or service env files.

options.title: Defer to env unification
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader environment-source cleanup and avoid a Kimi-specific fix until that contract is chosen.

recommendation.title: Make config env effective
recommendation.body: Materialize safe config env into the managed Gateway runtime/service context and update status, docs, and tests around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent visible history touches the central config/env and Gateway startup paths involved in this decision.
